explain.say: Here are your tools for stuck moments. One breath. A tiny first step. A five-minute timer. Or ask for help: Can you help me start, please? You are brave to try. Here is a challenge: next time you feel stuck, pick one tool.

zones.label: Stuck
zones.note: It feels too big to start.

tools.label: Ask for help
tools.ask: What can I say when I am stuck?

faq.a: A big job can feel heavy before you begin. Your brain wants to avoid the heavy feeling. Once you start, that feeling usually gets smaller.
asks: Tell me about It feels too big

faq.a: A tiny start is the smallest first bit, like writing your name, or doing just one sum. It gets you moving.
asks: Tell me about Just one sum
Tell me about Tiny first step

faq.q: What can I say when I am stuck?
faq.a: You can say, Can you help me start, please? or Can you do the first one with me? A grown-up you trust can help.
asks: Tell me about Ask for help

faq.q: How does a timer help me start?
faq.a: Set a timer for five minutes and say, I will only work until it rings. Five minutes feels small enough to begin.

faq.q: What if I still cannot start?
faq.a: That is okay. Take a short movement break, then try the tiny start again. Tell a grown-up how it feels.

facts: Breaking a job into a tiny first step is a common way to get started.
A slow breath out can help the body feel calmer.
